organism_context: Pulmonate gastropods (Helix pomatia albumen gland); the activity is the basis of EC 2.4.1.205
rationale: The only characterisation is a crude albumen-gland membrane activity transferring Gal from UDP-Gal onto galactogen; no protein was purified and no gene has ever been cloned, so bi/polyfunctionality cannot be assessed. Note the ModelSEED name says beta-1,4 while the EC and synonyms say beta-1,6.
direction_note: ModelSEED dropped the galactan acceptor that KEGG R00506 carries on both sides, leaving 'UDP-galactose -> UDP' with a galactosyl unit vanishing; a Leloir NDP-sugar donor step is physiologically one-way (UDP-Gal consumed), so the '<' recommendation is backwards.

organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis CSLA proteins expressed in insect cells); CSLA is the GT2 processive mannan synthase
rationale: Heterologous expression showed CslA family members alone encode GDP-mannose-dependent mannan synthase activity: a single processive GT2 polypeptide with one glycosyl-transfer active site. No second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: The mannan acceptor/product pair was stripped, so the entry reads 'GDP-mannose -> GDP' with a mannosyl unit unaccounted for; the real donor step is effectively irreversible toward GDP release.

enzyme_name: 4-chlorobenzoyl-CoA dehalogenase (FcbB), acting within the three-enzyme fcb dehalogenation pathway
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. CBS3, Arthrobacter sp. SU, and other 4-chlorobenzoate degraders
rationale: No single enzyme performs the free-acid reaction as written: 4-chlorobenzoate is first ligated to CoA (FcbA), the aryl-CoA thioester is hydrolytically dehalogenated by the monofunctional homotrimeric dehalogenase FcbB, and FcbC (a hotdog-fold thioesterase) releases 4-hydroxybenzoate. IUBMB has deleted EC 3.8.1.6 with the note that this activity 'has been shown to be identical to EC 3.8.1.7' (4-chlorobenzoyl-CoA dehalogenase).
direction_note: The pathway is irreversible toward 4-hydroxybenzoate, but its irreversibility comes from ATP/CoA activation and thioester hydrolysis that the lumped free-acid equation hides, so ModelSEED's '<' has no enzymological support.

organism_context: Neisseria polysaccharea amylosucrase; Leuconostoc mesenteroides / Streptococcus mutans dextransucrases
rationale: Both candidate enzymes behind this entry are non-Leloir glucansucrases with a single catalytic (beta/alpha)8 barrel and one catalytic triad; sucrose hydrolysis and transglucosylation are the same chemistry on different acceptors, not a second activity. The three ECs stacked on this entry (2.4.1.4/2.4.1.5/2.4.1.125) are all single-active-site glucansucrases.
direction_note: The glucan acceptor and the transferred glucosyl unit are both missing, reducing the entry to 'sucrose -> fructose'; glucansucrases run one-way from sucrose because the glucose-fructose glycosidic bond (~-27 kJ/mol) drives glucosyl transfer, so '<' is wrong.

enzyme_name: camphene synthase (class I monoterpene synthase, TPS-b)
organism_context: Conifers and Lamiaceae (e.g. Abies grandis, Salvia); camphene arises from the bornyl/pinyl cation branch of monoterpene synthases
rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry (GPP to camphene) because the ModelSEED entry carries no EC, KEGG or MetaCyc xref; plant monoterpene synthases are single-domain class I terpene cyclases with one Mg2+-dependent active site. Multiproduct behaviour (several terpene skeletons from one ionisation event) is one catalytic activity, not multifunctionality.
direction_note: Diphosphate is missing from the products, so the written equation hides the ionisation/PPi-release step that makes terpene cyclisation irreversible in the GPP -> camphene direction.

organism_context: Reported only as a crude activity in Neurospora crassa (and surveyed in Bdellovibrio and Streptomyces polyP studies)
rationale: The EC rests entirely on two 1971 Kulaev-lab reports of an activity in Neurospora crassa extracts; no protein has been purified, no gene cloned, and no structure or sequence exists, so functionality cannot be judged. KEGG still carries the EC as active (created 1976) with no comment.
direction_note: Polyphosphate is absent from both sides, so the entry reads '1,3-BPG -> 3-phosphoglycerate' with a phosphoryl group vanishing; the only reported physiology is polyP synthesis from the high-energy acyl phosphate, which runs left-to-right, but the unidentified enzyme makes this a weak call.

organism_context: Fungi (Saccharomyces CHS1-3, Aspergillus chsA-G), insects and nematodes
rationale: Chitin synthase is a single-polypeptide processive GT2 membrane glycosyltransferase with one UDP-GlcNAc active site. Fungal class V/VI enzymes (e.g. A. nidulans CsmA) carry an N-terminal myosin motor-like domain, but it serves actin-dependent localisation rather than a demonstrated second catalytic activity, so this stays monofunctional.
direction_note: The chitin acceptor/product pair was stripped, leaving 'UDP-GlcNAc -> UDP'; chitin synthase is a one-way polymerising enzyme and no reverse chitin phosphorolysis to UDP-GlcNAc exists.

enzyme_name: glycogen synthase (GlgA) / starch synthase (ADP-glucose dependent, EC 2.4.1.21)
organism_context: Bacteria (E. coli GlgA) and plant plastids (soluble and granule-bound starch synthases)
rationale: GlgA/starch synthases are single-active-site GT5 retaining glycosyltransferases that only elongate alpha-1,4 chains; branching (GlgB) and debranching are separate proteins. Called from well-established general enzymology, no literature search needed.
direction_note: The glucan acceptor and transferred glucosyl unit are missing ('ADP-glucose -> ADP'); ADP-glucose-dependent elongation is physiologically irreversible, so '<' (ADP -> ADP-glucose) would wrongly let models regenerate the sugar nucleotide.

enzyme_name: arabinan arabinosyltransferase (UDP-L-arabinofuranose:arabinan alpha-L-arabinofuranosyltransferase; no EC assigned)
organism_context: Plant Golgi (pectic arabinan biosynthesis); ARAD1/GT47-family proteins are candidates but lack direct biochemical demonstration
rationale: KEGG R03078 is 'UDP-L-arabinofuranose + arabinan = arabinan + UDP' with no ENZYME field and no EC; the activity is known only from plant membrane preparations, and the catalytic protein has not been established. Identity therefore cannot support a functionality call.
direction_note: The arabinan acceptor was stripped from both sides, leaving 'UDP-L-arabinose -> UDP'; a Leloir sugar-nucleotide donor step runs one way, toward UDP.

enzyme_name: alginate polymerase catalytic subunit Alg8 (mannuronan synthase, EC 2.4.1.33)
organism_context: Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Azotobacter vinelandii; Alg8 is the GT2 catalytic subunit of an Alg8/Alg44/AlgK/AlgX envelope complex
rationale: Alg8 is the single GT2 glycosyltransferase that polymerises GDP-mannuronate; Alg44 is a separate c-di-GMP-binding copurifying protein required for activity, i.e. a multi-protein machine rather than a fused bifunctional chain. Per the protocol exclusion, the catalytic subunit is scored monofunctional.
direction_note: The poly(mannuronate) acceptor is missing, so only 'GDP-mannuronate -> GDP' remains; periplasmic polymerisation and export make the real step one-way.

enzyme_name: keratan sulfate Gal-6-sulfotransferase (KSGal6ST / CHST1), with CHST6 (corneal GlcNAc6ST) for the GlcNAc-6 position
organism_context: Human/mammalian Golgi; cornea and cartilage keratan sulfate biosynthesis
rationale: The cloned KSGal6ST is a type II Golgi membrane protein with a single PAPS-binding sulfotransferase domain and no second catalytic activity; its only reported breadth is acceptor promiscuity (sialyl-LacNAc, fetuin glycans), which is one activity. The bifunctional enzyme in this pathway is PAPS synthase, which makes the cosubstrate, not this reaction.
direction_note: Both the keratan acceptor and the transferred sulfuryl group are stripped, leaving 'PAPS -> PAP'; PAPS-dependent sulfotransfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically irreversible toward PAP.

organism_context: Plants, algae, fungi and some bacteria; SMTs that act on a delta-24 sterol such as desmosterol give 24-methylenecholesterol
rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry (SAM-dependent C-24 methylation of a delta-24 sterol) since KEGG R03725 carries no ENZYME/EC field; SMTs are single-domain Class I SAM methyltransferases. Some SMTs catalyse successive C24 and C28 methylations, but that is one catalytic activity applied twice, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: The equation is balanced and sound; SAM-dependent methyl transfer with SAH release is essentially irreversible left-to-right, so ModelSEED's '<' (regenerating SAM from SAH) is not enzymologically possible.

enzyme_name: NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO1), with VKORC1/VKORC1L1 as the thiol-dependent alternative vitamin K quinone reductase
organism_context: Mammalian (mouse/human) vitamin K cycle; NQO1 is cytosolic, VKORC1/L1 are ER membrane enzymes
rationale: Both candidate enzymes behind EC 1.6.5.- for this step are single-activity oxidoreductases: NQO1 is an obligate two-electron FAD quinone reductase, VKORC1/VKORC1L1 are CXXC thiol-disulfide quinone/epoxide reductases. NQO1's reported p53/20S-proteasome interaction is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: The two electrons (NAD(P)H or the CXXC dithiol) are missing and only 2 H+ remain, so the equation is charge-unbalanced and its direction is set by whatever reductant was dropped; the enzyme class named (1.6.5.-, quinone reductase) runs K1 -> hydroquinone, i.e. left-to-right.

organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae Golgi; MNN4 is a positive transcriptional/regulatory partner, not a second catalytic subunit
rationale: MNN6, a KRE2/MNT1 (GT15) family type II Golgi membrane protein, was shown to be the gene for mannosylphosphate transfer onto cell-wall mannan, with one catalytic domain. MNN4 and MNN14 modulate the level of the modification rather than adding a second activity.
direction_note: The phosphomannan acceptor and the transferred mannosyl-phosphate are stripped, leaving 'GDP-mannose -> GMP'; transfer of mannose-1-phosphate with GMP release is one-way.

organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis, Plantago/psyllium, Physcomitrella); IRX10 works within an IRX9/IRX10/IRX14 Golgi xylan synthase complex
rationale: Heterologously expressed IRX10 and its psyllium/moss orthologues are themselves xylan xylosyltransferases with a single GT47 catalytic domain; IRX9 and IRX14 are separate polypeptides in the synthase complex, which the protocol excludes from 'bifunctional'. No second catalytic activity is reported for IRX10.
direction_note: The xylan acceptor is stripped so only 'UDP-xylose -> UDP' remains; Leloir xylosyl transfer to the growing chain is irreversible toward UDP.

enzyme_name: wall teichoic acid poly(glycerol phosphate) polymerase TagF (EC 2.7.8.12)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis 168 (purified recombinant enzyme, crystal structure solved); TagB is the separate priming enzyme
rationale: Purified recombinant TagF catalyses only the polymerisation of glycerol phosphate from CDP-glycerol onto the lipid III acceptor, and its structure shows a single catalytic centre with two essential histidines. Priming is done by the distinct protein TagB, so there is no fused second activity.
direction_note: The poly(glycerophosphate) acceptor and transferred glycerophosphate are missing, leaving 'CDP-glycerol -> CMP'; CDP-alcohol phosphotransfer with CMP release is physiologically one-way.

enzyme_name: poly(ribitol phosphate) polymerase TarL (CDP-ribitol:poly(ribitol phosphate) ribitolphosphotransferase, EC 2.7.8.14)
organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus late-stage wall teichoic acid biosynthesis (TarK/TarL paralogues in NCTC8325)
rationale: TarL is often described as 'bifunctional primase/polymerase', but both steps are the same CDP-ribitol-dependent ribitol-phosphate transfer chemistry applied to different acceptors (linkage unit vs growing chain), which the protocol's definition does not count as two distinct catalytic activities. There is one TagF-like catalytic domain.
direction_note: The polymer acceptor and transferred ribitol-phosphate are stripped, leaving 'CDP-ribitol -> CMP'; polymerisation with CMP release runs one way.

organism_context: Human/mammalian nucleus; plant orthologues exist (AraCyc/BrachyCyc xrefs)
rationale: PARP1 is multidomain (Zn1/Zn2/Zn3 fingers, BRCT, WGR, HD, ART) but carries a single catalytic ART site that performs initiation, elongation and branching of the same ADP-ribosyl transfer chemistry; the DNA-binding and automodification domains are regulatory, not catalytic. Degradation of the polymer is done by a separate enzyme, PARG.
direction_note: The protein/poly(ADP-ribose) acceptor is absent, leaving 'NAD+ -> nicotinamide + H+'; cleavage of the nicotinamide-ribosyl bond (dG'~ -34 kJ/mol) makes PARylation irreversible, and nicotinamide is a product inhibitor, never a substrate for resynthesis here.

organism_context: Lactobacillus reuteri 121 and L. johnsonii NCC 533 inulosucrases; Bacillus subtilis SacB levansucrase
rationale: The crystal structure of Lactobacillus inulosucrase shows a single five-bladed beta-propeller GH68 catalytic domain with one -1 fructosyl subsite; hydrolysis and transfructosylation are the same catalytic step with water or fructan as acceptor. No second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: The fructan acceptor and transferred fructosyl unit are stripped, leaving 'sucrose -> D-glucose'; the sucrose glycosidic bond energy drives transfructosylation one way, so '<' (glucose -> sucrose) is wrong.

organism_context: Bifunctional in E. coli and most bacteria (one folC gene product carries both activities); monofunctional FPGS in Lactobacillus casei and in mammals, where DHFS does not exist
rationale: Cloning and purification of the single E. coli folC gene product showed one polypeptide carrying both dihydrofolate synthetase (adding the first glutamate to dihydropteroate) and folylpolyglutamate synthetase (adding further gamma-glutamates to reduced folates). The L. casei enzyme, cloned separately, has only the FPGS activity.
direction_note: Both FolC activities are ATP-dependent amide ligations that run in the ATP -> ADP + Pi direction, so bifunctionality does not explain the conflict; the folate substrate/product pair is simply missing from the equation, which reduces it to a bare ATP hydrolysis that ModelSEED then points backwards.

organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana Golgi; GAUT1 is the catalytic GT8 subunit of a GAUT1:GAUT7 (or GAUT5/6) heterocomplex
rationale: GAUT1 carries the single galacturonosyltransferase active site; GAUT7 is a separate polypeptide that supplies the Golgi membrane anchor after GAUT1's transmembrane domain is proteolytically removed. That is a multi-subunit complex, which the protocol excludes from 'bifunctional'.
direction_note: The homogalacturonan acceptor is stripped, leaving 'UDP-galacturonate -> UDP'; GAUT1 polymerisation is one-way toward UDP release.

enzyme_name: class A penicillin-binding protein PBP1a/PBP1b (peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase, EC 2.4.1.129)
organism_context: E. coli PBP1a/PBP1b and their homologues across bacteria; monofunctional glycosyltransferases (MtgA) and the unrelated SEDS proteins RodA/FtsW also run this step
rationale: Class A PBPs are single polymorphic polypeptides carrying both an N-terminal GT51 transglycosylase domain that polymerises lipid II and a C-terminal penicillin-binding transpeptidase domain that crosslinks the stem peptides. Monofunctional alternatives exist (MtgA, RodA/FtsW), so the lineage matters, but the canonical EC 2.4.1.129 enzyme is genuinely bifunctional.
direction_note: The growing glycan-chain acceptor is missing, leaving a lipid-II-to-bactoprenyl-diphosphate stub; both PBP domains act only in the biosynthetic direction, driven by release of undecaprenyl pyrophosphate, so the reverse call has no support.

organism_context: Plant plastids and cyanobacteria; distinct from the bacterial/fungal CrtI which performs all four desaturations
rationale: Plant-type PDS is a single FAD-dependent desaturase that introduces two successive double bonds (phytoene to phytofluene to zeta-carotene) with plastoquinone as the electron acceptor; two rounds of the same catalytic activity is not bifunctionality. Reoxidation of plastoquinol is done by the separate plastid terminal oxidase.
direction_note: Free H2 stands in for the FAD/plastoquinone electron acceptor, which is exactly why eQuilibrator scores it reverse; the real redox partner is reoxidised by PTOX/O2, making desaturation irreversibly forward.

enzyme_name: phytoene desaturase (PDS), plant/cyanobacterial type - second desaturation (phytofluene to zeta-carotene)
organism_context: Plant plastids and cyanobacteria; same enzyme as rxn06784
rationale: The same single FAD-dependent PDS polypeptide performs this second desaturation, using plastoquinone as acceptor; repeating one catalytic activity on a more desaturated substrate does not make it bi- or polyfunctional.
direction_note: As with rxn06784, free H2 replaces the plastoquinone/FAD couple, so the thermodynamic sign that drives ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of the stripped acceptor rather than real enzymology.

enzyme_name: hyaluronan synthase (HAS, Class I: HAS1/2/3, bacterial spHAS/seHAS; EC 2.4.1.212)
organism_context: Vertebrate HAS1-3 and streptococcal spHAS/seHAS (Class I); Chlorella virus and Pasteurella Class II HAS differ in domain arrangement
rationale: Class I hyaluronan synthases are single membrane-embedded polypeptides that alternately transfer GlcNAc (beta-1,4) and GlcA (beta-1,3) onto the growing chain, i.e. two distinct glycosyltransferase activities in one chain; the 2023 DeAngelis and Zimmer review titles them 'unique bifunctional glycosyltransferases'. Both activities are needed for a single catalytic cycle.
direction_note: Only one UDP is released in the equation although two sugar nucleotides are consumed, and UDP-glucuronate is wrongly placed in the extracellular compartment (which also mis-flags the entry as a transport reaction); both HAS activities polymerise in the same direction, so '<' is unsupportable.
